key_insight: Relay contact welding can silently undermine student-built emergency-stop circuits despite a successful commissioning test.
engineering_relevance: Workshop safety assurance should prioritize integrity monitoring sensitive to welded contacts rather than rely solely on initial functional testing.
method: Model the emergency-stop circuit as a series safety function degraded by contact welding.
Derive conditions under which welded contacts cause an undetected failure on a demanded stop.
Simulate a before-after-control-impact estimator across cluster counts and intervention effect sizes.
evidence_signal: Across 2,000 replications per design cell with 8–32 clusters and 3–8-percentage-point effects, the analysis estimated that detecting a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power requires 54 clusters.
watch_item: The power estimate depends on declared variance assumptions; the abstract does not report physical fault-injection results or measured operator injuries.
paper_title: Functional-Safety-Integrity Degradation of Student-Built Emergency-Stop Circuits in Engineering Technology Education Workshops: A Fault-Injection Evaluation Linking Relay Contact Welding to Operator Injury-Risk Exposure
